title: Faster work, different workers
hook: If output rises after piece pay, how much came from who joined?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Decompose an observed productivity increase into worker effort and workforce selection.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Decompose an observed productivity increase into worker effort and workforce selection.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy firm’s output index rises from 100 to 144, with 22 units from within-worker change and 22 from workforce selection. What share of the 44-unit gain is selection? Toy inputs A=[100, 22, 22]; B=[100, 44, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[144, 22, 50], [144, 44, 0]]. Labels: Final output, Within gain, Selection share %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The total improvement can combine changed behavior by existing workers and a changed workforce. The comparison assigns the same total gain entirely to within-worker change. An aggregate percentage alone cannot identify that decomposition.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Baseline output=100, Within-worker gain=44, Selection gain=0. What is Selection share %? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Baseline output=100, Within-worker gain=44, Selection gain=0. What is Selection share %?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Switching Safelite windshield installers to piece rates raised productivity 44%, about half from attracting faster workers (Lazear, 2000).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Decompose an observed productivity increase into worker effort and workforce selection.
